svg.text: A30 · Difference amplifier
Subtract two signals
Post-16 · ages 16–19
Four matched resistor ratios make a difference amplifier. This
arrangement rejects a voltage that is shared by both inputs.
Your investigation
Predict OUT = SECOND − SIGNAL. Increase both input offsets by the
same amount, then deliberately mismatch a resistor and compare.
This activity
Compare differential excitation with equal voltages on both inputs.
Deliberately change one resistor to investigate imperfect common-mode
rejection.
Getting started
Open the Simulation tab and press Run. Select a source or component to
see its values. Read the labelled signals, then change one quantity at a
time. Equal net labels identify connected points.
Explain:
Use an equation, a truth table or a state sequence to justify your
prediction. Include units and discuss the model assumptions.
The model predicts electrical behaviour; it does not replace real practical
measurements.
